quick: Start 400 mg once daily, titrate by 400-600 mg weekly to maintenance 800-1,600 mg once daily
May be taken with or without food; whole or crushed
Limited data; animal developmental toxicity/malformations - weigh benefit vs risk, enroll in registry
Excreted in milk in animals; weigh benefit of breastfeeding against risk
Not recommended in severe hepatic impairment
Serum sodium (hyponatremia), suicidality/mood, LFTs, skin reactions, neurologic status
summary: Eslicarbazepine acetate is a once-daily antiepileptic indicated for partial-onset (focal) seizures in patients 4 years and older, as monotherapy or adjunctive therapy. It is a prodrug extensively converted to eslicarbazepine, the active moiety, which is thought to act by stabilizing the inactivated state of voltage-gated sodium channels. Important safety issues include hyponatremia, suicidal behavior and ideation (an antiepileptic class effect), serious dermatologic reactions and DRESS/multiorgan hypersensitivity, anaphylaxis and angioedema, neurologic effects (dizziness, somnolence, ataxia, diplopia), drug-induced liver injury and rare hematologic effects. It can reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives and interacts with several other antiepileptics and CYP2C19/CYP3A4 substrates.
indications: Treatment of partial-onset (focal) seizures in patients 4 years of age and older, as monotherapy or adjunctive therapy

dosage.d: 400 mg once daily (may start at 800 mg once daily if rapid seizure control outweighs risk)
dosage.n: Initiating at 800 mg increases risk of adverse reactions

dosage.d: Increase in weekly increments of 400-600 mg to 800-1,600 mg once daily
dosage.n: Titrate to clinical response and tolerability

dosage.d: Initiate and titrate weight-based once daily per labeling, increasing weekly to maintenance
dosage.n: Dosing depends on age, weight and renal function
Use not recommended in severe hepatic impairment
Abrupt withdrawal risks increased seizure frequency and status epilepticus

admin: Administer orally once daily, with or without food
Tablets may be swallowed whole or crushed
Titrate gradually (weekly increments) to reduce adverse reactions
Reduce the dose by 50% in moderate to severe renal impairment
Withdraw gradually rather than abruptly to avoid rebound seizures or status epilepticus
moa: Eslicarbazepine acetate is extensively converted to eslicarbazepine, considered the moiety responsible for therapeutic effect. The precise anticonvulsant mechanism is unknown but is thought to involve inhibition of voltage-gated sodium channels, stabilizing their inactivated state and thereby reducing repetitive neuronal firing and the spread of seizure activity.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to eslicarbazepine acetate or to oxcarbazepine
relative: History of severe cutaneous adverse reactions to related agents
Pre-existing hyponatremia or risk factors for it
Concomitant use with strong sodium-channel-blocking AEDs (additive CNS toxicity)
monitor: Patients on CYP2C19 substrates (e.g. phenytoin, omeprazole, clobazam)
Patients with depression or suicidal ideation

preg: Limited human data are insufficient to inform a drug-associated risk. In pregnant mice, rats and rabbits, eslicarbazepine acetate caused developmental toxicity including malformations (mice), embryolethality (rats) and fetal growth retardation at clinically relevant doses. Advise pregnant women of the potential risk to the fetus and encourage enrollment in the North American Antiepileptic Drug Pregnancy Registry. It may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives.
lact: Eslicarbazepine is excreted in animal milk; data in humans are limited. Consider the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding alongside the mother's clinical need and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed infant.
renal: In patients with moderate to severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance below 50 mL/min), reduce the dose by 50%. Standard hemodialysis partially clears the drug, so dosing may need consideration in dialysis patients.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is needed in mild to moderate hepatic impairment. Use is not recommended in severe hepatic impairment because of insufficient data. Discontinue if there is jaundice or evidence of significant drug-induced liver injury.

major: Other sodium-channel-blocking AEDs (e.g. carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine) - additive neurotoxicity; may also need mutual dose adjustment
Enzyme-inducing AEDs (carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, primidone) - reduce eslicarbazepine levels; higher doses may be needed
moderate: Phenytoin - eslicarbazepine inhibits CYP2C19 raising phenytoin levels while phenytoin lowers eslicarbazepine; adjust both
Clobazam and omeprazole (CYP2C19 substrates) - increased levels
CYP3A4 substrates including hormonal contraceptives and simvastatin - eslicarbazepine induces CYP3A4, lowering their levels
Warfarin - eslicarbazepine can alter exposure; monitor INR
minor: Drugs that lower serum sodium (e.g. diuretics) - additive hyponatremia risk
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol because of additive CNS depression.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor serum sodium for hyponatremia; abnormal thyroid function tests (reduced T3/T4) can occur.

serious: Serious dermatologic reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis)
Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)/multiorgan hypersensitivity

monitoring: Serum sodium at baseline and during therapy, especially with symptoms or risk factors for hyponatremia
Emergence or worsening of depression, suicidal thoughts or behavior, and mood changes
Signs of serious skin reactions, DRESS or hypersensitivity
Liver function tests if signs of hepatic injury appear
Complete blood count if hematologic adverse reactions are suspected
Neurologic status (dizziness, gait, vision); levels of interacting AEDs
counsel: Take once daily and do not stop suddenly - stopping abruptly can cause seizures
This medicine can cause dizziness, sleepiness and double or blurred vision; be careful with driving and machinery
Tell your doctor right away about thoughts of self-harm, depression or unusual mood changes
Seek urgent care for any rash, blistering, mouth sores, facial swelling or fever
Hormonal birth control may be less effective - use an additional method
Report nausea, headache, drowsiness or confusion that could signal low blood sodium
pk: Steady-state plasma concentrations attained after 4-5 days of once-daily dosing
Eslicarbazepine Tmax about 1-4 hours after dosing
Apparent half-life of eslicarbazepine about 13-20 hours in adult epilepsy patients
Once-daily dosing supported by the long half-life
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); keep tightly closed
pearls: Once-daily dosing is a practical advantage among sodium-channel-blocking antiepileptics
Reduce dose by 50% when creatinine clearance is below 50 mL/min
Check baseline and periodic serum sodium - hyponatremia can be significant
Induces CYP3A4 and can reduce hormonal contraceptive efficacy; advise additional contraception
Avoid abrupt discontinuation; taper to prevent rebound seizures and status epilepticus
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and take the next one at the usual time. Do not take two doses at once. Do not stop the medicine without talking to your doctor.
overdose: Symptoms of overdose mirror known adverse reactions and include hyponatremia (sometimes severe), dizziness, nausea, vomiting, somnolence, euphoria, oral paraesthesia, ataxia, gait difficulty and diplopia. There is no specific antidote; provide symptomatic and supportive treatment. Gastric lavage and/or activated charcoal may be considered early, and standard hemodialysis partially clears the drug and may be considered in significant renal impairment or severe overdose.
